behaviors.source: GH #334 AC4 (prd.md "Attempt Execution and Failure Semantics"; src/preserve-work-recovery.ts:1161; src/run-state.ts:284-341)
behaviors.given: three unresolved targets in one run-state file: a first whose trailing event is `PENDING` and whose published snapshot still holds the accepted pair; a second whose trailing event is `PENDING` and whose snapshot `contract.md` has been deleted so the restore must fail; and a third whose trailing event is `ROLLBACK_FAILED` and whose snapshot is still unreadable so its retry fails again
behaviors.when: `reconcileRecoveryLineage` runs once over that state, calling the existing `restoreAcceptedPairFromSnapshot` (`src/preserve-work-recovery.ts:1161`) with the trailing event's `RecoveryAttemptLocator` fields outside the lock, then — inside `transactRunState` (ADR 0056) — rereading state, rechecking that the trailing event is still the same `attemptId` in the same state, admitting the transition through `isLegalRecoveryTransition`, and appending through `appendRecoveryLineageEvent`
behaviors.then: the first target's pair is byte-restored and exactly one `ROLLED_BACK` event is appended for the same `attemptId`; the second target gets exactly one `ROLLBACK_FAILED` event appended for the same `attemptId`, carrying the restore failure message as `rollbackError` plus `observedContractFingerprint` and `observedManifestFingerprint` read off disk (an absent file recorded as #333's explicit absent marker, never a blank), with its destination pair left as it was; and the third target appends nothing, because `ROLLBACK_FAILED -> ROLLBACK_FAILED` is not a legal transition. Both append branches are obligations of this ID: the failing branch is the only place this slice writes the three `ROLLBACK_FAILED`-only fields (`src/run-state.ts:284-341`)
behaviors.observableResult: a test named `[behavior:#334:B-02]` asserts, for the first target, that its lineage grew by exactly one event whose `state` is `ROLLED_BACK` and whose `attemptId` equals the `PENDING` event's, and that both destination files are byte-identical to their snapshot copies; asserts, for the second target, that its lineage grew by exactly one event whose `state` is `ROLLBACK_FAILED`, whose `attemptId` equals its `PENDING` event's, whose `rollbackError` is non-blank and equal to the restore call's own failure message, and whose `observedContractFingerprint` and `observedManifestFingerprint` equal the values read from disk (the absent marker for the deleted file), and that its destination pair bytes are unchanged; asserts the third target's event list is unchanged event for event at every index; and asserts every appended event round-trips through save/load and that the reloaded file — not just the in-memory value — carries the appends, pinning that they happened inside the transaction

behaviors.given: four trailing-`PENDING` targets differing only in `snapshotPath`: a well-formed `<sliceDir>/recovery-snapshots/<attemptId>`; a two-segment `recovery-snapshots/<attemptId>`, whose grandparent is the empty string so the derived destination collapses onto `repoRoot`; a three-segment locator whose penultimate segment is not `recovery-snapshots`; and a single-segment locator. A `contract.md` and an `acceptance-manifest.json` of known bytes are planted at the repository root beforehand
behaviors.then: only the well-formed locator is resolved — its destination is the grandparent of the resolved snapshot directory, matching the locator `publishAcceptedPairSnapshot` builds as `relative(repoRoot, join(sliceDir, RECOVERY_SNAPSHOT_DIRNAME, attemptId))` (`src/preserve-work-recovery.ts:519-520,569`, `RECOVERY_SNAPSHOT_DIRNAME` = `recovery-snapshots` at `:86`). Each of the other three is rejected before any file is read or written, because the accepted form requires at least three segments, every segment non-empty and neither `.` nor `..`, the penultimate segment equal to `RECOVERY_SNAPSHOT_DIRNAME`, and hence a non-empty derived `<sliceDir>`. A rejected locator restores nothing, appends nothing, and is reported as a failed reconciliation naming the locator and the destination it would have derived
behaviors.observableResult: a test named `[behavior:#334:B-03]` asserts that after the call the repository-root `contract.md` and `acceptance-manifest.json` are byte-identical to the planted bytes — the assertion that fails if the two-segment locator's derived destination collapsed onto `repoRoot` — and that no file exists under `repoRoot` that did not exist before. For each rejected locator it asserts the target's lineage list is unchanged event for event, and that the reported outcome's message names both the rejected locator and the derived destination that caused the rejection, so the two-segment case is rejected for the derived-destination reason and not merely for segment count. For the well-formed locator it asserts the resolved destination equals `dirname(dirname(join(repoRoot, ...snapshotPath.split("/"))))` and that the restore landed there

behaviors.given: run state carrying a trailing PENDING event for a slice in scope and a recording stub provider
behaviors.then: reconciliation appends its event before ordinary resume decides anything: no provider invocation is recorded, no worktree is prepared and resume[ghIssue].attempts is unchanged
behaviors.observableResult: the stub provider recorded zero invocations, the lineage gained its terminal event, and the resume counter in the run-state file still reads its planted value

behaviors.given: the recovery fixture with unresolved lineage planted in run state and no live process, exercised once per reported outcome family: a target reconciled to `ROLLED_BACK`, a target reconciled to `ROLLBACK_FAILED`, and a target that appended nothing (a trailing `ROLLBACK_FAILED` whose retry failed again, and a rejected locator)
behaviors.when: `runPipeline` is invoked once with a recording stub provider
behaviors.then: it writes one `logger.phase(...)` line per reported target naming the target `ghIssue`, the appended outcome (`ROLLED_BACK`, `ROLLBACK_FAILED`, or that nothing was appended and why) and the retry fixed for that outcome — relaunch for `ROLLED_BACK`; repair the named snapshot directory then relaunch for a `ROLLBACK_FAILED` appended this launch; and for the append-nothing outcomes, that the hold is intentionally terminal until #335, naming the run-state file and the `attemptId` and saying a relaunch alone will report the same target and stop again — then returns `{ success: false, summary, consoleSummary, failureReason }` whose `failureReason` names the reconciled targets and says the launch stopped after reconciliation, dispatching no agent, resolving no run scope and moving no resume counter
behaviors.observableResult: a test named `[behavior:#334:B-05]` asserts `success` is `false` and `failureReason` contains each reported target's `ghIssue`; asserts `run.log` carries exactly one line per reported target; asserts, per outcome family, that the line contains the outcome name and the retry that outcome fixes — the snapshot directory path for the repair retries, and the run-state file path plus the `attemptId` plus the terminal-until-#335 statement for the append-nothing lines; and asserts the stub provider recorded zero invocations and `resume[ghIssue].attempts` is unchanged

behaviors.source: GH #334 AC7/AC8 (prd.md "No attempt changes from `ROLLED_BACK` or `ROLLBACK_FAILED` back to `PENDING`"); src/preserve-work-recovery.ts:644
behaviors.given: a target whose trailing event is `ROLLBACK_FAILED` and whose snapshot is still unreadable, and separately a target reconciled to `ROLLED_BACK`
behaviors.when: reconciliation runs over the first, and `admitStaleRenegotiation` (`src/preserve-work-recovery.ts:644`) runs for the second afterwards
behaviors.then: reconciliation is append-only: it never edits or deletes a prior lineage event, never writes inside a published snapshot directory, and never rewrites a prior attempt's `attemptId`. The failing retry appends nothing, because `ROLLBACK_FAILED -> ROLLBACK_FAILED` is not a legal transition, so the existing hold stays in force; after the `ROLLED_BACK` append, `admitStaleRenegotiation` is no longer blocked by `hasOpenRecoveryAttempt` and mints a new `attemptId` and a new snapshot directory
behaviors.observableResult: a test named `[behavior:#334:B-06]` asserts every prior event is still present byte-for-byte at its original index, asserts a digest of each published snapshot directory is unchanged across the call, asserts the failing-retry target's list length is unchanged and `recoveryDispatchRefusal` still returns a refusal for it, and asserts the fresh admission produces an event whose `attemptId` differs from the reconciled one and whose `snapshotPath` names a different directory while the prior snapshot directory's contents are untouched
